# Contact-constrained weighted surface repair without charging active cells twice

This note extends the common-affine projective-weighted surface repair to
a finite concave minimum L=min_i A_i, under a precise contact hypothesis
on the OLD endpoint coupling. The proof works by restricting one global
optimizer according to its OUTPUT cells. It does not independently
rebuild preassigned source-cell couplings.

Dependencies:

* `candidate 1dcb5bc1e68b837f`;
* `candidate 9764a982661d3ddc`;
* the mixed variable-density optimizer and measurable-assembly theorems
  cited in those notes.

No OC statement follows here. In particular the required contact for
an actual physical surface flow must be proved separately.

## 1. Data and the additional contact condition

Use a finite lattice-complete compatible family of positive
d-dimensional fibers K_z, with d>=1, canonical convex hull C, and
normal-bundle surface measure eta. All physical coordinates are
w=(z,x). Let

    L(w)=min_(1<=i<=N) A_i(w)>0 on C,

where A_i are affine. Thus L is a continuous positive concave
piecewise-affine function. Since C is compact, L has a positive
minimum. In particular every A_i is positive on C.

At each normal u let H(u,w) be a common concave physical function,
with the bounded Borel weight

    W(u,w)=H(u,w)_+/L(w)^d.

The same statement permits normal-dependent finite affine families
provided the contact gap and the final weighted reference are Borel;
no measurable active-plane choices are needed in the assembly below.
For clarity the proof is written with the fixed family above. Put
omega=W eta.

Let gamma_-,gamma_+<=omega have equal finite mass. Suppose an old
endpoint coupling has:

1. the same normal at its two endpoints;
2. integer midpoints lying on the actual target support graph;
3. exact L-Jensen contact almost everywhere:

    L((w_-+w_+)/2)=[L(w_-)+L(w_+)]/2.             (1)

Then there exists another same-normal coupling with the same endpoint
marginals, retaining (1) and the actual support graph, whose midpoint
law rho satisfies

    rho<=2^n omega.

Within each normal and original parity class its midpoint law is above
the old law in full physical convex order. The usual marked-source
reconstruction is also available.

The positivity and bounded-weight assumptions are explicit. The note
does not pass this statement through vanishing L, singular weights, or
a rate limit without a separate limiting argument.

## 2. Two finite contact partitions at one normal

Fix one normal outside the common exceptional sets of the surface
density theorem, and one parity class. The endpoint conditional
measures have equal mass. All product endpoint bases have integer
midpoints in the complete base set.

Let h_z be the actual support heights in this normal. The finite-base
roof construction gives a globally finite concave piecewise-affine
function

    h_tilde(z)=min_(1<=k<=Q) B_k(z),

agreeing with h_z at every sampled base. Every endpoint under
consideration satisfies u dot x=h_tilde(z). For a pair of endpoints
define the nonnegative continuous gaps

    J_L=L(mid)-[L(w_-)+L(w_+)]/2,
    J_h=h_tilde(midbase)
                    -[h_tilde(z_-)+h_tilde(z_+)]/2.

The actual support-graph condition is exactly J_h=0. Thus the allowed
coupling class consists of the fixed-marginal couplings concentrated
on the closed set

    E={J_L=J_h=0}.                                  (2)

It is nonempty because it contains the old coupling, and is compact
and convex.

Define closed convex physical cells

    C_i={w in C:A_i(w)=L(w)},
    D_k={w in C:B_k(z)=h_tilde(z)}.

Convexity follows directly from their affine inequalities
A_i<=A_j and B_k<=B_l. At an output midpoint choose the least active
index i for L and the least active index k for h_tilde. This gives a
finite disjoint Borel partition of all outputs, including all ties.

**Contact observation.** If a tuple in E has output in the (i,k)
part of this partition, then BOTH endpoints belong to C_i intersect
D_k.

Indeed A_i>=L and equality at the midpoint, together with J_L=0,
gives

    [A_i(w_-)-L(w_-)] + [A_i(w_+)-L(w_+)]=0.

Both terms are nonnegative, so both vanish. The identical argument
with B_k and J_h proves endpoint membership in D_k.

Conversely, any two endpoints in the same C_i intersect D_k satisfy
both contact equalities: concavity bounds each midpoint value below
its active affine upper plane and above the average of the endpoint
values, which coincide. This remains true at cell interfaces and for
any reassignment of base pairs within the same parity class.

## 3. The restriction of the optimizer is an unrestricted optimizer

Maximize the integral of a smooth globally strongly convex function
of the physical midpoint over the compact class (2). Let pi be one
optimizer. Partition THIS pi by its canonical output (i,k), writing
pi=sum_(i,k) pi_ik.

The endpoint marginals of pi_ik are supported in the closed compact
sets C_i intersect D_k within the original endpoint supports.
Although the canonical output part itself need not be closed, taking
the support of either restricted endpoint marginal does not leave
those closed cells.

Every coupling of those restricted endpoint marginals is supported
in (C_i intersect D_k)^2. By the contact observation it satisfies (2),
and it preserves the original parity. Replacing pi_ik by any such
coupling therefore preserves global feasibility and all full endpoint
marginals.

Consequently pi_ik is an UNRESTRICTED strong-surplus optimizer for
its own endpoint marginals. Otherwise a better unrestricted coupling
would improve pi, contradicting its constrained global optimality.

This is the central point. We only analyze the existing restrictions;
we do not rebuild them separately and then assert that their output
labels remain disjoint.

## 4. Affine-weighted density control of every restricted optimizer

On C_i the original weight is exactly H_+/A_i^d. The restricted
endpoint submeasures are thus dominated by the full reference
surface measures weighted by the COMMON positive affine denominator
A_i and the common concave numerator H. They vanish outside C_i, so
this domination holds on the whole original endpoint fibers.

Every product pair of their supports is also in D_k, and therefore
has actual target support contact. The conditional ball theorem gives
the common target face dimension and tangent space. The
projectively weighted envelope with denominator A_i applies to every
marginal-good pair:

    F_target >= N_m(F_-,F_+)       when m>0,

and its atom/minimum version applies when m=0.

Because pi_ik is already an unrestricted strong-surplus optimizer,
the inverse-endpoint-map and weighted area-formula proof applies to
pi_ik ITSELF. It yields

    midpoint_*pi_ik <= (H_+/A_i^d) eta_target.

This is the optimizer-level conclusion of the density-selection
proof, not merely the existence of some alternative capped coupling.
Its actual output is in C_i; there A_i=L. Thus this restricted
midpoint law is dominated by omega_target.

The actual restricted midpoint laws are supported on the mutually
disjoint canonical output parts used to define them. If these parts
are E_ik, then for every Borel set A,

    sum_(i,k) rho_ik(A)
      =sum_(i,k) rho_ik(A intersect E_ik)
      <=sum_(i,k) omega_target(A intersect E_ik)
      <=omega_target(A).                            (3)

Hence the whole constrained optimizer has the desired ONE-copy
target density bound in the fixed parity class.

This argument includes positive conditional mass on tie faces.
Different affine planes can coincide identically on a target face;
the canonical output partition is still disjoint, and equation (3)
does not require those tie sets to be null.

## 5. One capped contact coupling dominates every old convex test

Within the fixed-marginal class (2), let D be the subclass whose
midpoint law is dominated by omega_target. It is convex and weakly
compact: both the contact support and domination by a fixed finite
Borel measure are weakly closed. It is nonempty by Sections 3--4.

For every finite convex test f, approximate f uniformly on the
compact output range by smooth strongly convex functions. Their
maximizers over (2) belong to D by (3), and their values are at least
the corresponding old-coupling values because the old coupling
belongs to (2). Compactness passes this comparison to f.

The usual finite-dimensional separation using nonnegative
combinations of finitely many convex tests, followed by compact
finite intersection, produces one pi in D such that

    rho_old<=cx midpoint_*pi.

The strong-surplus optimizations were performed over the contact
class (2), not over a class already constrained by old-law convex
order. The latter restriction would have invalidated the
unrestricted-piece argument.

## 6. Assembly, parity, and marks

The final pointwise constraints can be expressed entirely in physical
coordinates: fixed conditional marginals, zero integral of the
nonnegative continuous contact gap J_L, target domination, and the
countable convex-order tests. Target domination places all outputs
on the actual target normal bundle, so the roof contact need not be
encoded by a measurable choice of its facets.

These constraints define compact nonempty sets with Borel kernel
right sides. The established measurable-assembly lemma selects them
over normals. Summing the at most 2^n parity classes gives the
claimed global bound. There is no extra factor for the number of
L planes, support-roof facets, or coincident faces.

A martingale from each old midpoint law to its improved law can be
selected as before. Retaining the old mark, normal, parity, and
old-midpoint joint law, then drawing selected endpoints conditional
on their new midpoint, preserves the mark's conditional midpoint
mean and the exact endpoint marginals.

Since the final midpoint law and the endpoint marginal laws have
equal L integrals by (1), the old-to-new midpoint martingale also
has L-Jensen contact. This follows from concavity and equality of
the integrated Jensen inequality, rather than an additional
measurable plane label.

## 7. The actual-stress invariant still required

For a physical martingale from nu to eta, concavity always gives

    integral L dnu >= integral L deta.              (4)

Equality is equivalent to zero Jensen gap in almost every row.
When L=min_i A_i, every such row lies in each affine contact cell
active at its source: if A_i=L at the source, then
integral(A_i-L) over the row is zero.

The actual inverse-volume logarithmic contact rows in
`candidate 8ba63f3af7e6943f`
have this equality. Their marginals are not the physical surface
martingale marginals, so that fact cannot be silently transferred.

The ordinary normal-convex surface stress supplies (4), by testing
the finite convex function -L, but does not by itself turn it into
an equality. In the notation nu=(W/beta)eta, the missing scalar
condition is exactly

    integral L(W-beta) deta=0                       (5)

at the required normal conditioning. The currently known inequality
has the nonnegative sign. No claim is made here that (5) follows
from selected-minimum stationarity, deepestness, or cap criticality.

Thus this note solves the finite-cell overlap problem once actual
L-contact is available. It isolates a concrete scalar dissipation
whose vanishing, or quantified control, is the remaining interface
with the physical variational certificate.

## 8. Exact dissipation formula and a diagnostic on an existing stress

Let Pi(ds,dt)=nu(ds)P_s(dt) be any actual physical martingale on C.
Choose the least i with A_i(s)=L(s). Affine barycenter preservation
then gives the exact identity

    integral L dnu - integral L deta
      =sum_i integral_(source cell i)
             integral [A_i(t)-L(t)] P_s(dt) nu(ds).          (6)

Every integrand is nonnegative. Therefore zero dissipation is
equivalent to almost every source row remaining in every active
contact cell of its source. Formula (6) retains the actual martingale
and its cross-cell targets; it is not an arbitrary partition of the
target surface measure.

The already existing eight-cap, three-square example in Section 4 of
`candidate 229cbb48c7fa3080`
provides a useful exact diagnostic. It has beta=19/36 and an actual
same-normal martingale from nu=(W/beta)eta to eta. Take

    L(z,X)=1-epsilon |X_1|
          =min(1-epsilon X_1,1+epsilon X_1),
    0<epsilon<1.

On either horizontal normal face, with tangent coordinate t=X_1,
summing the source-minus-target measures across the three bases gives

    dnu-deta=[-3/19+(9/19)1_(|t|<1/3)]dt,
    -1<=t<=1.

The constant part of L integrates to zero. Since
integral_[-1,1] |t| dt=1 and integral_[-1/3,1/3] |t|dt=1/9,

    integral L(dnu-deta)=2epsilon/19>0.

Equivalently the scalar surface dissipation in (5) is epsilon/18
at each horizontal normal. At the two vertical normals L is constant
on the face, and the dissipation vanishes. The total is epsilon/9.

This computation does not create a new selected-minimum example:
the existing square construction is not asserted to satisfy the
logarithmic parameter stationarity with this L. It proves only the
precise limitation needed here: an actual cap law, an actual physical
surface martingale, and the ordinary convex stress alone do not force
(5). A further identity from the selected parameter problem must
eliminate or pay the nonnegative quantity (6).
